title: How Bearing Rate Helps Solve the Puzzle
summary: Discover how the rate at which a bearing changes reveals the contact's position relative to your own track.
objectives: Identify when a bearing is changing quickly vs slowly
Relate bearing rate to the contact's relative geometry
Use two bearing observations separated by time to estimate bearing rate
Submit a course estimate and compare it to truth

tasks.title: First Bearing
tasks.description: A contact is detected on bearing 045°. Before advancing time, predict: will the bearing drift toward 000° or toward 090°?

tasks.title: Observe Bearing Rate
tasks.description: Advance time and watch the bearing change. At what simulated time does the bearing pass through due north (0°)? What does that tell you about the closest point of approach?

tasks.title: Estimate Course
tasks.description: Based on the bearing history you have observed, submit your best estimate for the contact's course in degrees true.

hints.text: The ownship is heading east and the contact is coming from the northeast. The bearing to a target on your port bow will shift left (toward 000°) as you get closer.
When the bearing changes most slowly, the contact is near the closest point of approach. Fast bearing change means the contact is crossing your bow or stern.
If the bearing rate is roughly constant, the contact is on a steady course. Extrapolate from two widely separated bearings to guess the contact's course.

debriefRules.feedback: Consider how the bearing shifted over time. A leftward drift means the contact was to your port side moving westward.
The speed of bearing change is related to how close the contact passes. Short CPA = fast bearing rate early on.
